spans.s:
yáva, m. orig. prob. any grain or corn,
yielding flour; later, barley-corn, barley.
[cf. ζειά, *ζαϝ-ιά, ‘corn.’]

yava-madhyama, a. having a barley.
corn middle, i. e. big in the middle and
small at the ends, like a creseendo-diminnendo
sign; as n. the Yavamadhyama,
name of a cāndrāyaṇa or lunar penance.
[1297, 1280b.]

yáviṣṭha, a. youngest; esp. of a fire just
born of the sticks of attrition or just set
on the altar. [superl. to yúvan, q. v., but
from the simpler *yu, 468.]

yáviṣṭhya, a. = yaviṣṭha, but always at
the end of a pāda and as diiambus.

yávīyāṃs, a. younger. [comp. to
yúvan, q. v., but from the simpler *yu,
468.]

yā́vant [517],
 —1. a. as great, 101^9; as
many, 64^4, 105^4; as much; preceding its
correl. tāvant;
 —2. yā́vat, adv. as long,
while; tāvat…yāvat, so long…as,
19^2, 42^3; yāvat…tāvat: as long
as…, so long, 15^5, 32^2, 40^18; as soon
as or the moment that…, then, 44^15,
22^7;
 —3. yāvat, as quasi-prep. w. acc.:
during; up to (in space or time); sarpavivaraṃ
yāvat, as far as the serpent's
hole, 39^13; adya yāvat, until to-day,
24^2. [pron. root ya, 517: cf. tāvant.]

yāvayád-dveṣas, a. driving away foes.
[√2yu, ‘keep off’: see 1309.]
